# Comparison objective and training-budget scope

[Home](../../README.md) · [Documentation](../README.md) · [All experiments](../experiments/README.md)

**Experimental objective.** RoboSeed studies model behavior under practical, limited-hardware training budgets, using the ABot-M0 downstream study as the comparison reference. Some official training recipes require resources beyond this setting, so local runs adapt their batch sizes, training durations and execution settings to the available hardware. The goal is to compare models at comparable downstream training scales. The recorded runs below retain their actual budgets; batch size, updates, sample exposure and compute are not all equal across families. A local score below a released checkpoint therefore describes this budget-adapted recipe and does not establish that the original method is weaker.

## What is being compared

The scientific question is how different models perform at comparable downstream training scales on practical hardware, with ABot-M0 as the reference experiment. Official large-scale training requirements can exceed the resources available for this study; we therefore adapt local recipes and report their actual costs and outcomes. A lower local score is an observation about that configuration and budget, not a verdict on the original model or its full official training procedure.

The present snapshot is an ABot-M0-referenced, budget-conscious comparison. Exact equalization remains a study objective: the existing runs have different update counts, batches, training units and inherited priors. They must not be described as an already completed equal-FLOP, equal-exposure or equal-GPU-hour experiment.

## Actual downstream training scale

| Local model | Hardware / stopping point | Global batch | Recorded sample exposure | H200 training GPU-hours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ABot-M0 reference · six backbones | 4 H200 NVL; 150k updates | 64 | 9.60M examples per backbone | 174.126–509.207 |
| LingBot-VLA 2.0 | 3 H200; 50k updates | 96 | 4.80M windows | 174.365 |
| OpenWAM | 4 H200 NVL; 80k updates | 64 | 5.12M video windows | 262.068 |
| LiLa-WAM | Saved stage-1 epoch 12 / stage-2 epoch 4 | See package configuration | Not normalized to an ABot-equivalent count | Not independently verified |

The measured few-GPU runs use H200-class accelerators; the recorded device types and GPU counts define the practical hardware scope of this snapshot. Sample exposure is batch × updates where available. An ABot example, a LingBot window and an OpenWAM video window contain different observations and have different compute costs. Reported H200 intervals cover downstream adaptation, excluding inherited foundation pre-train and unmetered setup, failed trials or engineering work.

## How to read the reference rows

**Released weights** means an official checkpoint evaluated through our local, family-specific execution path. **Local budget run** means our checkpoint trained with an adapted recipe. These references are evaluated locally; they are not original-paper leaderboard numbers. Within a family, official and local weights share the documented local evaluator. Across families, observations, action semantics, task conditioning and evaluation coverage still differ.

LingBot uses 4.8M local windows against 51.2M in the source recipe; OpenWAM uses 5.12M against an estimated 30.376M. LiLa is evaluated at the saved stage-2 epoch-four checkpoint, with five episodes per task and visual task tokens. Keep these differences next to any score comparison and preserve the complete task counts.

## Rules for future comparisons

Declare the matched budget variable before training: for example, downstream allocated GPU-hours on the same accelerator, or sample exposure within a compatible training representation. Record the ABot-M0 reference, allowed hardware, batch, updates, precision, initialization and data coverage. Publish remaining mismatches, evaluator revisions and task denominators. Do not substitute the original paper’s larger-scale result for a locally evaluated reference, or attribute a budget-dependent difference to architecture alone.
